28549.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
28549.text: The first ionization enthalpies of Be , B , N and O follow the order
28549.sol: The ionisation enthalpy increases as we go from left to right in a period, while it decreases as we come down a group. So according to this, the order will be Be < B < C < N < O . But there are two exceptions, in the case of Be and N because of the highly stable 2 s 2 (completely filled orbital) and 2 s 2 2 p 3 (half-filled orbital 2 p 3 ) valence configuration. Due to this, the correct order is: B < Be < C < O < N .

potential difference remains the same and energy increases n times.

Each capacitor retains its charge CV , so the series combination carries total charge Q_s = CV . The resulting potential difference is V_s = Q_s / C_s = CV / (C/n) = nV . 71198.text: The umbilical cord in human females is formed of three blood vessels which are ___.
options: two small arteries and one large vein
two small veins and one large artery.
71198.sol: The umbilical cord connects the developing fetus to the placenta. It contains three blood vessels: two umbilical arteries and one umbilical vein. The two umbilical arteries are smaller in diameter and carry deoxygenated blood along with waste products from the fetus to the placenta. 80498.text: Functional megaspore in an angiosperm develops into:
80498.sol: Megaspore is the first cell of the female gametophytic generation in angiosperm. It is formed from the megaspore mother cell by meiosis. Out of the four cells created, only one megaspore develops, and remaining three degenerates. The formation of the female gametophyte from a single functional megaspore is called as monosporic development. It undergoes three successive generations of free nuclear mitosis to form 8-nucleated and 7-celled embryo sac.

120621.subject: Chemistry
120621.text: What is the main storage polysaccharide of plants?
120621.sol: Starch is the main storage polysaccharide of plants.

120879.subject: Chemistry
120879.text: The correct order of match between column X and column Y is
120879.sol: The correct match is I-(iii), II-iv, III-i, IV-ii. I. Vitamin A - (iii) Night blindness II. Vitamin D - (iv) Osteomalacia III. Vitamin E -(i) Muscular weakness IV. Vitamin K - (ii) Blood clotting time

121534.subject: Botany
121534.text: An association between roots of higher plants and fungi is called
121534.sol: An association between roots of higher plants and fungi is called Mycorrhiza.

121583.subject: Botany
121583.text: An organism is observed to be unicellular and lacks a nuclear membrane. Further analysis reveals that it completely lacks a cell wall and is among the smallest known living cells. Which of the following groups does this organism belong to?
121583.sol: The absence of a nuclear membrane indicates that the organism is a prokaryote, which eliminates slime moulds as they are eukaryotic protists. Among prokaryotes, Mycoplasma are unique because they completely lack a cell wall. They are also recognized as the smallest living cells known. Archaebacteria and cyanobacteria are prokaryotes, but they both possess a cell wall. Therefore, the described organism belongs to Mycoplasma. Answer: Mycoplasma

121686.subject: Botany
121686.text: What is Numerical Taxonomy based on?
121686.sol: At present phylogenetic classification systems based on evolutionary relationships between the various organisms are acceptable. This assumes that organisms belonging to the same taxa have a common ancestor. We now use information from many other sources too to help resolve difficulties in classification. These become more important when there is no supporting fossil evidence. Numerical Taxonomy which is now easily carried out using computers is based on all observable characteristics . Numbers and codes are assign

121759.subject: Botany
121759.text: Which of the following is not a common member of red algae?
121759.sol: The members of rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas. They occur in both well-lighted regions close to the surface of water and also at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates.The red thalli of most of the red algae are multicellular. Some of them have complex body organization. The food is stored as floridean starch wh

121955.subject: Botany
121955.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The broad classification of living organisms under the system was proposed by Whittaker in 1969. 2. He suggested the Three Kingdom classification. 3. Fungi, and the members of the Monera and Protista are still classified under Kingdom Plantae. 4. Plantae though earlier classifications placed them in the same kingdom. 5. The latest systems of classificati
121955.sol: Fungi, and members of the Monera and Protista having cell walls have now been excluded from Plantae though earlier classifications placed them in the same kingdom. So, the cyanobacteria that are also referred to as blue green algae are not ‘algae’ any more. The earliest systems of classification used only gross superficial morphological characters such as habit, colour, number and shape of leaves, etc.

122077.subject: Botany
122077.text: Top-shaped multiciliate male gametes, and the mature seed which bears only one embryo with two cotyledons, are characterised features of:
122077.sol: Cycads are the gymnosperm having largest top shaped multiciliate male gametes. Conifers have sperm that do not have flagella, but instead are conveyed to the egg via a pollen tube. It is important to note that the seeds of gymnosperms are not enclosed in their final state upon the cone.

122347.subject: Botany
122347.text: Select the correct statement about these organisms.
options: They exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic.
They have a central gastro-vascular cavity with two openings, mouth on hypostome
They exhibit three basic body forms
122347.sol: Cnidarians exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic. They have a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening, mouth on hypostome. Digestion is extracellular and intracellular. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa

122382.subject: Botany
122382.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates Reason: Vertebrates possess notochord in their adult stage and all chordates possess a vertebral column
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
122382.sol: The members of subphylum Vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period. The notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult. Thus all vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.

122446.subject: Botany
122446.text: Type of symmetry and body organization Phylum A. Asymmetrical, cellular organization 1. Sponges B. Radial symmetry, tissue level of organization 2. Ctenophores C. Radial symmetry, tissue level of organization with comb plates 3. Cnidarians D. Bilateral symmetry, organ level of organization 4. Platyhelminthes
122446.sol: Sponges are asymmetrical with cellular organization. Cnidarians are radially symmetrical with a tissue level of organization. Ctenophores are also radially symmetrical with comb plates. Platyhelminthes are bilaterally symmetrical with organ level of organization.

122777.subject: Botany
122777.text: Select A, B, C, D and E from the following diagram
options: Node, Internode, Primary Root, Secondary Root, Root System
Internode, Node, Primary Root, Secondary Root, Root System
Internode, Node, Primary Root, Secondary Root, Shoot System

123061.subject: Botany
123061.text: Leaves become modified into spines in:
123061.sol: Opuntia leaves get modified into spines to protect them from grazing animals, also reduce the area of transpiration. In this condition, the stem gets modified to phylloclade and performs photosynthesis. Pea leaves are modified into tendrils. Onion leaves become fleshy to store food in them. Silk cotton gets modified from unifoliate leaves to multifoliate leaves.

123062.subject: Botany
123062.text: In China rose the flowers are
123062.sol: Actinomorphic (star-shaped) can be divided into 3 or more identical sectors, which are related to each other by rotation about the centre of the flower, e.g., China rose. Zygomorphic flowers can be divided by only a single plane into two mirror image halves, e.g., orchids. Valvate aestivation The sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, e.g., Calotropis. Twisted aestivation One margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one, e.g., China rose. Imbricate aestivation the margins of sepa

123079.subject: Botany
123079.text: Which one of the following is a xerophytic plant in which the stem is modified into the flat green and succulent structure?
123079.sol: Opuntia is a plant growing in dry and xeric habitats. In this, the stem having several nodes and internodes is modified into flat, fleshy, thick, green leaf-like structure called phylloclade. Phylloclade performs the function of photosynthesis like a leaf and also stores food. The leaves get modified into spines which helps to reduce transpiration.

123328.subject: Botany
123328.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1.The xylem and phloem patches in roots are surrounded by conjuctive tissue. 2.The parenchymatous cells between the xylem and the phloem are called conjuctive tissue. 3.The pith is located between the xylem and the phloem. 4.The endodermis is called the conjuctive tissue.
123328.sol: The parenchymatous cells which lie between the xylem and the phloem are called conjuctive tissue. There are usually two to four xylem and phloem patches.

123976.subject: Botany
123976.text: What are the unique structures found in prokaryotic cells?
123976.sol: No organelles, like the ones in eukaryotes, are found in prokaryotic cells except for ribosomes. Prokaryotes have something unique in the form of inclusions . A specialized differentiated form of cell membrane called mesosome is the characteristic of prokaryotes. They are essentially infoldings of cell membrane

124230.subject: Botany
124230.text: Mitochondrial Functions Characteristics A. ATP Production 1. Increases the surface area for reactions B. DNA Presence 2. Contains the genetic material C. Ribosomes 3. Site of cellular energy production D. Cristae 4. Involved in protein synthesis
124230.sol: ATP production is the main function of mitochondria, DNA is present in the matrix, ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis, and cristae increase the surface area for reactions.

124625.subject: Botany
124625.text: What does a and b denote?
options: a- Heterophylly in buttercup, b- Heterophylly in larkspur
a- Heterophylly in buttercup, b- Heterophylly in cotton
Heterophylly in larkspur, b- Heterophylly in buttercup
Heterophylly in larkspur, b- Heterophylly in cotton

124783.subject: Botany
124783.text: Match List I with List II. List I List II A. 2,4-D I. Rooting in stem cuttings B. IBA II. Hastening fruit ripening C. Ethephon III. Increasing sugarcane yield D. Gibberellic acid IV. Preparing weed-free lawns Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
124783.sol: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin widely used to kill dicotyledonous weeds, thus helping in preparing weed-free lawns. IBA (Indole-3-butyric acid) is an auxin used to initiate rooting in stem cuttings. Ethephon is a widely used source of ethylene that hastens fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples. Gibberellic acid is sprayed on sugarcane crops to increase the length of the stem, thereby increasing the yield. Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III. Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

124809.subject: Botany
124809.text: Refer the given figures on photoperiodism and select the correct option.

124816.subject: Botany
124816.text: Assertion : Senescence is the time when age associated defects are manifested. Reason : Certain genes may be undergoing sequential switching on and off during one's life.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If both Assertion and Reason are false.
124816.sol: Process of ageing is called senescence. Ageing, is cumulative changes in an organism, organ, tissue, or cell leading to a decrease in functional capacity. In humans, aging is associated with degenerative changes in the skin, bones, heart, blood vessels, lungs, nerves, and other organs and tissues. It is genetically controlled programme regulated by regulatory genes. This view is suggested by the great range of lifespans among different animal speciesfrom a few days in the fruit fly to more than 100 years in some to

125120.subject: Botany
125120.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. The F1 headpiece is a peripheral membrane protein complex and contains the site for synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. 2. F1 is an integral membrane protein complex that forms the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane. 3. The passage of protons through the channel is coupled to the catalytic site of the F0 component for t
125120.sol: The F1 headpiece is a peripheral membrane protein complex and contains the site for synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. F0 is an integral membrane protein complex that forms the channel through which protons cross the inner membrane. The passage of protons through the channel is coupled to the catalytic site of the F1 component for the production of ATP. For each ATP produced, 4H+ passes through F0 from the intermembrane space to the matrix down the electrochemical proton gradient.

125144.subject: Botany
125144.text: Organic substrates that are oxidised during respiration to liberate energy inside the living cells are called ___.
125144.sol: Organic substrates that are oxidised during respiration to liberate energy inside the living cells are called Respiratory substrates

125379.subject: Botany
125379.text: When the two photosystems work in a series, what is the process called?
125379.sol: Living organisms have the capability of extracting energy from oxidisable substances and store this in the form of bond energy. Special substances like ATP, carry this energy in their chemical bonds. The process through which ATP is synthesised by cells (in mitochondria and chloroplasts) is named phosphorylation. Photophosphorylation is the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light. When the two photosystems work in a series, first PS II and then the PS I, a process called non-cycli

125654.subject: Botany
125654.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): During photosynthesis, ATP and NADPH produced in the light reaction diffuse out of the chloroplast to provide energy for various cellular processes. Reason (R): ATP and NADPH are required to drive the biosynthetic phase occurring in the stroma of the chloroplast. In the light of the above statement
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
125654.sol: Assertion (A) is false because ATP and NADPH produced during the light reaction do not diffuse out of the chloroplast to power general cellular processes. Oxygen is the only product of the light reaction that diffuses out of the chloroplast into the surrounding environment. Reason (R) is true because the assimilatory powers (ATP and NADPH) are strictly retained within the chloroplast and utilized to drive the biosynthetic phase (Calvin cycle) for CO ₂ fixation, which takes place in the stroma. Answer: (A) is false

125669.subject: Botany
125669.text: How many additional ATP molecules are required by a C₄ plant compared to a C₃ plant for the synthesis of one molecule of glucose?
125669.sol: In C₃ plants, the fixation of one CO ₂ molecule via the Calvin cycle requires 3 ATP molecules. To synthesize one molecule of glucose (which requires 6 CO ₂ molecules), a C₃ plant consumes 6 3 = 18 ATP molecules. In C₄ plants, the initial fixation of one CO ₂ molecule in the mesophyll cells requires 2 extra ATP molecules (to regenerate PEP), bringing the total to 5 ATP molecules per CO ₂ fixed. To synthesize one molecule of glucose, a C₄ plant consumes 6 5 = 30 ATP molecules. The additional number of ATP molecules r

125897.subject: Botany
125897.text: What type of water-pollinated plants have ribbon-like pollen grains?
125897.sol: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most of the land plants. In Vallisneria, the female flower reach the surface of water by the long stalk and the male flowers or pollen grains are released on to the surface of water. They are carried passively by water some of them eventually reach

126153.subject: Botany
126153.text: Components of Pollen Grain Features A. Generative Cel 1. Larger and spindle shaped nucleus B. Intine 2. Sporopollenin C. Vegetative Cell 3. Smaller D. Exine 4. Pectocellulose
126153.sol: The hard outer layer called the exine is made up of sporopollenin which is one of the most resistant organic material known. Pollen grains are wellpreserved as fossils because of the presence of sporopollenin. The inner wall of the pollen grain is called the intine. It is a thin and continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin. When the pollen grain is mature it contains two cells, the vegetative cell and generative cell (Figure 2.5b). The vegetative cell is bigger, has abundant food reserve and a large irregul

126979.subject: Botany
126979.text: In the stratosphere, which of the following elements acts as a catalyst in degradation of ozone and release of molecular oxygen?
126979.sol: In the stratosphere, Cl acts as a catalyst in degradation of ozone and release of molecular oxygen. UV rays act on CFCs to release Cl atoms which speed up the degradation of the ozone. This cycle continues to hamper the ozone layer leading to its depletion.

127160.subject: Botany
127160.text: What is the greatest biodiversity on earth?
options: Amazonian rain forest in South America
127160.sol: A forest in a tropical region like Equador has up to 10 times as many species of vascular plants as a forest of equal area in a temperate region like the Midwest of the USA. The largely tropical Amazonian rain forest in South America has the greatest biodiversity on earth- it is home to more than 40,000 species of plants, 3,000 of fishes, 1,300 of birds, 427 of mammals, 427 of amphibians, 378 of reptiles and of more than 1,25,000 invertebrates. Scientists estimate that in these rain forests there might be at least

127181.subject: Botany
127181.text: How does species richness affect year:to:year variation in total biomass according to Tilman's long:term ecosystem experiments?
options: Plots with more species showed more year:to:year variation in total biomass
Plots with more species showed less year:to:year variation in total biomass
There was no relationship between species richness and year:to:year variation in total biomass
The relationship between species richness and year:to:year variation in total biomass was not determined
127181.sol: A stable community should not show too much variation in productivity from year to year; it must be either resistant or resilient to occasional disturbances (natural or man-made), and it must also be resistant to invasions by alien species. We don’t know how these attributes are linked to species richness in a community, but David Tilman’s long-term ecosystem experiments using outdoor plots provide some tentative answers. Tilman found that plots with more species showed less year-to-year variation in total biomass.

127330.subject: Botany
127330.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. In situ conservation is used when an ecosystem needs to be conserved as a whole. 2. Ex situ conservation is a method where species are conserved outside their natural habitat. 3. The Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro highlighted the need for global biodiversity conservation. 4. India has 14 national parks and 448 biosphere reserves.
127330.sol: Earth Summit, also known as the Convention on Biological Diversity, was held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 and called upon all nations to take measures for the conservation of biodiversity and the sustainable utilization of its benefits. The other statements are incorrect because ex situ conservation involves conserving species outside their natural habitat, and in situ conservation is the method used to conserve ecosystems as a whole. Additionally, India has 14 biosphere reserves, 90 national parks, and 448 wildlife s

127746.subject: Botany
127746.text: The major reservoir of carbon on earth is ___.
127746.sol: The major reservoir of carbon on earth is sea

128542.subject: Zoology
128542.text: Chemical Nature of Hormone Hormone A. Amino-acid derivatives 1. FSH B. Iodothyronines 2. T3 C. Steroids 3. Adrenaline D. Peptide, polypeptide, protein 4. Cortisol
128542.sol: (i) peptide, polypeptide, protein hormones (e.g., insulin, glucagon, pituitary hormones, hypothalamic hormones, etc.) (ii) steroids (e.g., cortisol, testosterone, estradiol and progesterone) (iii) iodothyronines (thyroid hormones) (iv) amino-acid derivatives (e.g., epinephrine).

128585.subject: Zoology
128585.text: When a person consumes a large amount of water, it significantly increases their body fluid volume. Which of the following correctly describes the subsequent physiological changes regarding the state of osmoreceptors, ADH release, and diuresis, respectively?
128585.sol: An increase in body fluid volume due to excess water consumption switches off (suppresses) the osmoreceptors. This suppression halts the stimulation of the hypothalamus, leading to a decrease in the release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) from the neurohypophysis. Without the action of ADH, water reabsorption in the latter parts of the renal tubules decreases, which results in enhanced diuresis (increased urine volume). Option 1 is incorrect because fluid loss, not fluid gain, activates osmoreceptors. Option 3 is inc

128696.subject: Zoology
128696.text: Assertion : Auerbach's plexus controls the secretion of intestinal juice. Reason : Meissner's plexus controls the peristalsis in alimentary canal.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
128696.sol: Auerbach's plexus is a network of nerve cell and parasympathetic nerve fibre present in the muscularis layer of wall of alimentary canal. It controls peristalsis. On the other hand, Meissner's plexus is a network of nerve cells and sympathetic nerve fibre present in the submucosa layer of wall of alimentary canal. It controls the secretion of intestinal juice.

128842.subject: Zoology
128842.text: Which type of circulatory system is more advantageous?
128842.sol: The circulatory patterns are of two types – open or closed. Open circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs in which blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities called sinuses. Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system in which the blood pumped by the heart is always circulated through a closed network of blood vessels. This pattern is considered to be more advantageous as the flow of fluid can be more precisely regulated .

129573.subject: Zoology
129573.text: What is the primary function of sweat produced by sweat glands?
options: Facilitating a cooling effect on the body surface
Providing a protective oily covering for the skin
129573.sol: The sweat and sebaceous glands in the skin can eliminate certain substances through their secretions. Sweat produced by the sweat glands is a watery fluid containing NaCl, small amounts of urea, lactic acid, etc. Though the primary function of sweat is to facilitate a cooling effect on the body surface , it also helps in the removal of some of the wastes mentioned above. Sebaceous glands eliminate certain substances like sterols, hydrocarbons and waxes through sebum. This secretion provides a protective oily coveri

129759.subject: Zoology
129759.text: Which one is component of Ornithine cycle?
129759.sol: Ornithine cycle or urea cycle or Krebs-Henseleit cycle was discovered by Hans Krebs and Kurt Henseleit. It takes place in liver cells. The main component of ornithine cycle are arginine, ornithine and citrulline.

129813.subject: Zoology
129813.text: What happens when the intra-pulmonary pressure is equal to atmospheric pressure?
129813.sol: When the intra-pulmonary pressure is equal to atmospheric pressure, neither inspiration nor expiration occurs . Breathing involves two stages : inspiration during which atmospheric air is drawn in and expiration by which the alveolar air is released out.The movement of air into and out of the lungs is carried out by creating a pressure gradient between the lungs and the atmosphere. Inspiration can occur if the pressure within the lungs (intra-pulmonary pressure) is less than the atmospheric pressure, i.e., there is

130352.subject: Zoology
130352.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Clavicle forms hip bone Reason: Each clavicle is a long slender bone with three curvatures.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
130352.sol: Each clavicle is a long slender bone with two curvatures. This bone is commonly called the collar bone.

130660.subject: Zoology
130660.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: India was among the first countries in the world to initiate reproductive health programmes at a national level Reason: The programmes called ‘family planning’ were initiated in 1951 and were periodically assessed over the past decades.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
130660.sol: India was amongst the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes at a national level to attain total reproductive health as a social goal. These programmes called ‘family planning’ were initiated in 1951 and were periodically assessed over the past decades.

130898.subject: Zoology
130898.text: What is the result of the first meiotic division of the primary oocyte?
options: Formation of a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body
The formation of a mature follicle
The rupture of the Graafian follicle
130898.sol: The secondary follicle soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterized by a fluid filled cavity called antrum. The theca layer is organized into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa. It is important to draw your attention that it is at this stage that the primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle grows in size and completes its first meiotic division. It is an unequal division resulting in the formation of a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body. The secondary ooc

130902.subject: Zoology
130902.text: What is the number of primary follicles in the ovary at puberty?
130902.sol: The process of formation of a mature female gamete is called oogenesis which is markedly different from spermatogenesis. Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed within each fetal ovary; no more oogonia are formed and added after birth. These cells start division and enter into prophase-I of the meiotic division and get temporarily arrested at that stage, called primary oocytes. Each primary oocyte then gets surrounded by a layer

131340.subject: Zoology
131340.text: The early stage human embryo distinctly possesses

131481.subject: Zoology
131481.text: What was the purpose of the experiment performed by Meselson and Stahl?
options: To prove that DNA replicates semiconservatively
To show that 15N is not a radioactive isotope
To determine the density of DNA
To observe the effect of 15NH₄Cl on the growth of E. coli
131481.sol: It is now proved that DNA replicates semiconservatively . It was shown first in Escherichia coli and subsequently in higher organisms, such as plants and human cells. Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl performed the following experiment in 1958: (i) They grew E. coli in a medium containing 15NH4Cl (15N is the heavy isotope of nitrogen) as the only nitrogen source for many generations. The result was that 15N was incorporated into newly synthesized DNA (as well as other nitrogen containing compounds). This heavy DN

131613.subject: Zoology
131613.text: What is the definition of an allele?
131613.sol: As polymorphism in DNA sequence is the basis of genetic mapping of human genome as well as of DNA fingerprinting, it is essential that we understand what DNA polymorphism means in simple terms. Polymorphism (variation at genetic level) arises due to mutations. New mutations may arise in an individual either in somatic cells or in the germ cells (cells that generate gametes in sexually reproducing organisms). If a germ cell mutation does not seriously impair an individual's ability to have offspring who can transmit

131810.subject: Zoology
131810.text: Read the following statements carefully: (I) In bacteria, a single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyses transcription of all types of RNA. (II) Sigma ( ) factor is required for the termination of transcription in prokaryotes. (III) In eukaryotes, there are at least three RNA polymerases in the nucleus. (IV) Rho ( ) factor transiently associates with RNA polymerase to initiate transcription. How many of the above st
131810.sol: Statement (I) is correct as bacteria have a single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase that catalyses the transcription of mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA. Statement (II) is incorrect because the sigma ( ) factor is the initiation factor, not the termination factor. Statement (III) is correct as eukaryotes have a clear division of labour with at least three RNA polymerases (I, II, and III) in the nucleus (in addition to the RNA polymerase found in organelles). Statement (IV) is incorrect because the rho ( ) factor is the termination

132226.subject: Zoology
132226.text: What type of sex determination is exemplified by grasshoppers?
132226.sol: Due to the involvement of the X-chromosome in the determination of sex, it was designated to be the sex chromosome, and the rest of the chromosomes were named as autosomes. Grasshopper is an example of XO type of sex determination in which the males have only one X-chromosome besides the autosomes, whereas females have a pair of X-chromosomes.

132293.subject: Zoology
132293.text: How many chromosomes are present in a normal human cell?
132293.sol: The chromosomal disorders on the other hand are caused due to absence or excess or abnormal arrangement of one or more chromosomes. Failure of segregation of chromatids during cell division cycle results in the gain or loss of a chromosome(s), called aneuploidy. For example, Down’s syndrome results in the gain of extra copy of chromosome 21. Similarly, Turner’s syndrome results due to loss of an X chromosome in human females. Failure of cytokinesis after telophase stage of cell division results in an increase in a

132323.text: Identify and name x and y respectively.

132542.text: Assertion : Number of chromosomes in one genome is equal to number of linkage groups. Reason : Linkage groups give important information about the location of genes in the chromosomes.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.

132629.subject: Zoology
132629.text: Which of the following is a test cross ?
132629.sol: A test cross is a cross between heterozygous F ₁ hybrid and double recessive homozygous eg, Tt tt to show whether F ₁ is homozygous or heterozygous.

132665.subject: Zoology
132665.text: What type of atmosphere was present on early Earth ?

132833.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Darwin realised that there were many varieties of finches in the same Galapagos island. 2. From the original seed-eating features, many other forms with altered beaks arose, enabling them to become insectivorous and vegetarian finches 3. This process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and literally radi
132833.sol: All the varieties, he conjectured, evolved on the island itself. From the original seed-eating features, many other forms with altered beaks arose, enabling them to become insectivorous and vegetarian finches (Figure 6.5). This process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and literally radiating to other areas of geography (habitats) is called adaptive radiation. 133093.subject: Zoology
133093.text: The most recent and direct pre-historic ancestor is
133093.sol: The cro-magnon man (Homo sapiens fossalis) is the most recent and direct prehistoric ancestor of present man. It arose about 3,40,000 years ago.

133139.subject: Zoology
133139.text: What was the idea of health according to early Greeks and Indian Ayurveda system of medicine?
options: Health is a state of balance between body and mind
Health is determined by the amount of "black bile" in the body
Health is affected by neural and endocrine systems
Health is only influenced by genetic disorders
133139.sol: Early Greeks and Indian Ayurveda system of medicine believed that a person's health was determined by the balance of certain "humors" in the body, and that persons with "black bile" belonged to hot personality and would have fevers. William Harvey disproved the "good humor" hypothesis of health by discovering the blood circulation and demonstrating normal body temperature in persons with black bile using a thermometer. 133304.sol: Heroin is a depressant that slows down body functions.Heroin is usually taken by snorting and injection. Opioids are drugs that bind to specific opioid receptors present in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract. Excessive dosage of cocaine causes hallucinations.Cannabinoids are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system of the body.Coca Alkaloid or cocaine interferes with the transport of the neuro-transmitter dopamine.Natural cannabinoids are obtained from the inflorescences of the plant

133336.subject: Zoology
133336.text: Consider the following four statements (I-IV) regarding kidney transplant and select the two correct ones out of these. I. Even if a kidney transplant is proper the recipient may need to take immunosuppressants for a long time. II. The cell-mediated immune response is responsible for the graft rejection. III. The B-lymphocytes are responsible for rejection of the graft. IV. The acceptance or rejection of a kidney tra
133336.sol: Grafts from just any source – an animal, another primate, or any human beings cannot be made since the grafts would be rejected sooner or later. Tissue matching, blood group matching are essential before undertaking any graft/transplant and even after this the patient has to take immuno–suppresants all his/her life. The body is able to differentiate ‘self’ and ‘nonself’ and the cell-mediated immune response is responsible for the graft rejection.

133401.subject: Zoology
133401.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Carcinogens include substances like tobacco smoke and ionizing radiation. Reason: Carcinogens cause cancer by directly increasing the cell’s rate of division without damaging DNA.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
133401.sol: In our body, cell growth and differentiation is highly controlled and regulated. In cancer cells, there is breakdown of these regulatory mechanisms. Normal cells show a property called contact inhibition by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth. Cancer cells appears to have lost this property. As a result of this, cancerous cells just continue to divide giving rise to masses of cells called tumors. Tumors are of two types: benign and malignant. Benign tumors normally remain con

133476.subject: Zoology
133476.text: Effect Substance or Activity A. Mood swings and depression 1. Anabolic steroids B. Decreased sperm production 2. Chronic alcohol use C. Increased risk of AIDS 3. Intravenous drug use D. Deepening of voice in females 4. Anabolic drugs
133476.sol: Mood swings and depression can be side effects of anabolic steroid misuse. Anabolic steroid use in males can lead to decreased sperm production. Intravenous drug use increases the risk of contracting AIDS. Deepening of voice in females is a masculinizing effect of anabolic steroids.

134050.subject: Zoology
134050.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
134050.text: Which one is used in tissue culture?
134050.sol: Explant is used in plant tissue culture. It is an excised plant part which has the potential to give rise to whole new plant. The plants obtained through this technique are morphologically and genetically similar to each other and to their parent plant.

6a104ff98b46719ce7976cf5.text: An astronomical telescope is set in normal adjustment for viewing a distant object. The magnifying power of the telescope is 14 and the distance between the objective lens and the eyepiece is 105 cm . The focal lengths of the objective and the eyepiece are respectively:

Answer: 98 cm and 7 cm

6a13e466688ac6d0667aad1d.text: A nichrome heating element has a resistance of 100 at room temperature ( 20^ C ). When it is connected to a 220 V supply, a steady current of 2.0 A flows through it. If the temperature coefficient of resistance of nichrome averaged over the temperature range involved is 2.0 10⁻⁴ ^ C ⁻¹ , what is the steady temperature of the heating element?
6a13e466688ac6d0667aad1d.sol: Resistance at room temperature T₁ = 20^ C is R₁ = 100 . Resistance at steady temperature T₂ is R₂ = V I = 220 2.0 = 110 . Using the relation R₂ = R₁ [1 + (T₂ - T₁)] , we get: 110 = 100 [1 + 2.0 10⁻⁴ (T₂ - 20)] 1.1 = 1 + 2.0 10⁻⁴ (T₂ - 20) 0.1 = 2.0 10⁻⁴ (T₂ - 20) T₂ - 20 = 0.1 2.0 10⁻⁴ = 500 T₂ = 520^ C Answer: 520^ C

6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1e.subject: Biology
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1e.text: In the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase, which of the following metal ions acts as a cofactor by forming coordination bonds with side chains at the active site?
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1e.sol: Carboxypeptidase is a proteolytic enzyme that requires a metal ion cofactor for its catalytic activity. The active site of carboxypeptidase contains a Zn²⁺ ion, which forms coordination bonds with the side chains of specific amino acid residues (typically two histidine residues and one glutamate residue) and a water molecule. The Zn²⁺ ion plays a crucial role in polarizing the carbonyl oxygen of the peptide bond, making the carbonyl carbon more susceptible to nucleophilic attack during the hydrolysis of the peptide

95348.subject: Botany
95348.text: Diploblastic animal with radial symmetry is
95348.sol: Diploblasty is a condition of the blastula in which there are two primary germ layers: the ectoderm and endoderm. They do not show the mesodermal layer. Roundworms, earthworms and liver fluke have bilateral symmetry. These are elongated worm-like organisms. Hydra is radially-symmetrical. The body of the organism can be divided into equal halves in any plane of the axis. The tentacles radiate outward around the mouth. These type of arrangement of the tentacles gives the organisms a radial form of symmetry.

Nuclear envelope assembles around the chromosome clusters.

96897.subject: Botany
96897.text: Observe this floral diagram. What does the part denoted by the arrow indicate?
options: The position of bract in the flower
The position of petiole or stalk of the flower
The position of thalamus of the flower
The position of the mother axis with respect to the flower
96897.sol: A floral diagram provides information about the number of parts of a flower, their arrangement, and the relation they have with one another. The position of the mother axis with respect to the flower is represented by a dot on the top of the floral diagram. Calyx, corolla, androecium, and gynoecium are drawn in successive whorls, calyx being the outermost and the gynoecium being in the center. The floral formula also shows cohesion and adhesion within parts of whorls and between whorls.

96961.subject: Botany
96961.text: Select the CORRECT statement from the following: P In monocots, leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly Q In all leguminous plants, the leaf base may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus R The lamina or leaf blade is the green expanded part of the leaf with vein and veinlets S Veins provide rigidity to leaf blade
96961.sol: The leaf is divided into three parts - leaf base, petiole and lamina or leaf blade. Leaf base is a junction between the leaf and stem and in monocotyledons, it forms a sheath covering the stem completely or partially. In some leguminous plants, it swells up which is called a pulvinus. Petiole helps to hold the leaf blade allowing it to flutter in wind. The leaf blade is extended green part consisting of veins and veinlets which provide rigidity as well as transport food, water and minerals. In monocots, leaf base e

96993.subject: Botany
96993.text: All the statements about the members of the Liliaceae family are false except
options: The length of filaments in all stamens is the same.
They have leaves without stipules but show parallel venation.
They have a trilocular superior ovary with three ovules
They have fruits which are mostly berries and rarely capsule
96993.sol: Members of the Liliaceae family have 6 stamens, three with long stamens and three with short stamens. They have a tricarpellary, syncarpous gynoecium with an ovary which is superior, trilocular with many ovules and has axile placentation. They have fruits which are mostly capsules (dry and dehiscent) and rarely berries (Fleshy fruits). They also show alternate phyllotaxy with linearleaves without stipule and with parallel venation.

97007.subject: Botany
97007.sol: Drupe is a fleshy fruit that develops from either one or several fused carpels and contains one or many seeds. The seeds are enclosed by the hard protective endocarp (pericarp) of the fruit, e.g.,mango. In mango the pericarp is well differentiated into an outer thin epicarp, a middle fleshy edible mesocarp and an inner stony hard endocarp.

304666.text: Two periodic waves with amplitudes A₁ and A₂ travel through a region. Given that A₁ > A₂ , what is the difference between the maximum and minimum possible resultant amplitudes?
304666.sol: The resultant amplitude A of two waves with amplitudes A₁ and A₂ having a phase difference is given by A = A₁^2 + A₂^2 + 2A₁A₂ . The maximum resultant amplitude occurs when = 1 , which gives A_ max = A₁ + A₂ . The minimum resultant amplitude occurs when = -1 , which gives A_ min = |A₁ - A₂| . Since A₁ > A₂ , A_ min = A₁ - A₂ . The difference between the maximum and minimum resultant amplitudes is A_ max - A_ min = (A₁ + A₂) - (A₁ - A₂) = 2A₂ .

6a7a1ff82169692da504030d.text: A physical quantity P is related to three observables X , Y , and Z by the relation P = X^3 Y^2 Z . If the maximum percentage errors in the measurement of P , X , and Z are 15 % , 1 % , and 4 % respectively, then the percentage error in the measurement of Y is:
6a7a1ff82169692da504030d.sol: The relation for the physical quantity is given by P = X^3 Y^2 Z^ 1/2 . The maximum percentage error in P is given by the sum of the percentage errors of the individual quantities multiplied by their respective powers: P P 100 = 3 ( X X 100 ) + 2 ( Y Y 100 ) + 1 2 ( Z Z 100 ) Given that the percentage errors in P , X , and Z are 15 % , 1 % , and 4 % respectively, we can substitute these values into the equation: 15 = 3(1) + 2 ( Y Y 100 ) + 1 2 (4) 15 = 3 + 2 ( Y Y 100 ) + 2 15 = 5 + 2 ( Y Y 100 ) 2 ( Y Y 100 ) = 10

6a7a1ff8a734eb0e42690be5.text: Samples of the same ideal gas are kept in two separate containers. The ratio of the collision frequency of the gas molecules in the first container to that in the second container is 2 . If the ratio of the absolute temperature of the gas in the first container to that in the second container is 4 , then the ratio of their pressures is
6a7a1ff8a734eb0e42690be5.sol: The collision frequency of an ideal gas is given by Z = 2 d^2 n v Since the number density n = P kT and the average speed v = 8kT m , we can write the proportionality as: Z P T T P T For the same gas in two different states, the ratio of their collision frequencies is: Z₁ Z₂ = P₁ P₂ T₂ T₁ We are given that Z₁ Z₂ = 2 and T₁ T₂ = 4 . Substituting these values: 2 = P₁ P₂ 1 4 2 = P₁ P₂ 1 2 P₁ P₂ = 4 Answer: 4

6a7a1ff88212003916700564.text: A cell of emf 6 V and unknown internal resistance r is connected across a 4 resistor. A non-ideal voltmeter having a resistance of 12 is connected across the 4 resistor. If the voltmeter reads 3 V , the internal resistance r of the cell is _____ .
6a7a1ff88212003916700564.sol: The non-ideal voltmeter is connected in parallel with the 4 resistor. The equivalent resistance R_p of the voltmeter and the external resistor is: R_p = 4 12 4 + 12 = 48 16 = 3 The voltmeter reads the voltage across this parallel combination, which is V = 3 V . The total current I drawn from the cell is: I = V R_p = 3 3 = 1 A Using the equation for the complete circuit: E = I(R_p + r) 6 = 1 (3 + r) 3 + r = 6 r = 3 Answer: 3

6a7a1ff8abcc63daa0e28464.text: The reaction of (2R)-2-bromopentane with NaI is carried out to form a major product. Identify the stereochemistry of the major product formed. Furthermore, what will be the effect on the rate of this reaction if the solvent is changed from acetone to methanol?
options: Major product is (2S)-2-iodopentane; the reaction rate increases in methanol.
Major product is (2R)-2-iodopentane; the reaction rate decreases in methanol.
Major product is (2S)-2-iodopentane; the reaction rate decreases in methanol.
Major product is a racemic mixture of 2-iodopentane; the reaction rate increases in methanol.
6a7a1ff8abcc63daa0e28464.sol: The reaction of an alkyl halide with NaI is the Finkelstein reaction, which proceeds via an S _ N 2 mechanism. Since S _ N 2 reactions occur with complete inversion of configuration (Walden inversion), the nucleophile ( I ^- ) attacks from the side opposite to the leaving group ( Br ^- ). Because the relative priority of the groups around the chiral centre remains unchanged ( I > propyl > methyl > H ), the (2R)-2-bromopentane substrate is converted exclusively into (2S)-2-iodopentane.
